opening: Adam Dickie Glasgow belongs to the documented Ballymena family. The 1830–1840 newspaper sequence adds a strong, qualified candidate for his Broughshane education, Belfast Institution teaching and Berry Street ministry. It supplies no new parent or sibling proof. His father, John Glasgow-1657, is assessed at 96% through his brother James's journal and the Broughshane family monument.

biography_sections.title: Newspaper evidence and profile attribution
biography_sections.markdown:
The profile assignment remains qualified. Adam Dickie Glasgow-1781 (1815–1863), Presbyterian minister with a documented Belfast period, is the strongest compatible profile. Repeated Adam D. and the Institution setting support a consolidated education/teaching account; continuity into the Berry Street ministry is a supported inference. The inspected notices do not give Dickie in full, age, parents or later migration. The older Inishrush Adams remain separate namesake comparisons; no family link is upgraded.

Adam D. Glasgow of Broughshane appears in the Royal Belfast Academical Institution school prizes in June 1830 and Belfast College examinations reported in May 1831. The 1831 report also names James Glasgow, Institution, in voluntary advanced mathematical examinations. [Belfast News-Letter, 29 June 1830, p.3, Royal Belfast Academical Institution School Department](https://www.newspapers.com/image/390569859/) · [Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1831, p.3, Belfast College report dated 30 April](https://www.newspapers.com/image/390545285/)

Adam D. Glasgow resigned as an assistant in the Royal Belfast Institution’s Mathematical and Mercantile School in December 1836. Rev. Adam D. Glasgow received a unanimous call to Berry Street Presbyterian Church, Belfast, in January 1840 and was its newly ordained minister at a congregational presentation on 5 March. [Belfast News-Letter, 10 January 1837, p.2, resignation presentation on 22 December 1836](https://www.newspapers.com/image/390542489/) · [Belfast News-Letter, 17 January 1840, p.2, Berry Street ministerial call](https://www.newspapers.com/image/390553900/) · [Belfast News-Letter, 10 March 1840, p.2, Berry Street soiree on 5 March](https://www.newspapers.com/image/390555182/)

[Complete newspaper account and held draft](/research/subjects/newspapers-irish-1800-1850/#adam-belfast-education-ministry). Check Institution admissions/staff records and Berry Street call and ordination minutes for the full middle name, parents and earlier residence. Keep the already documented Ballymena sibling relationship separate from the newspaper assignment.

The live WikiTree profile checked on 4 October 2026 gives Ballymena as an uncertain birthplace. The older local imported vital field still says Lisburn; the recorded 19 August 2026 correction and its source basis remain in the research notes. The newspaper notices do not establish a birthplace.
